# Cornelia Bryant

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040), [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019)</sub>
- **Status:** Engaged  <sub>[v4 c37 P8](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0008), [v4 c37 P10](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0010)</sub>
- **Origin:** Four Winds  <sub>[v4 c6 P37](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0037), [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Miss Cornelia  <sub>[v4 c6 P37](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0037), [v4 c8 P15](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0015)</sub>

## Appearance

She has a fresh, round, pink-and-white face with jolly, kindly brown eyes. She wears a hard little knob of fair hair held in place by a tight elastic band around her head. She carries herself with dignity despite wearing unusual attire such as calico print wrappers and aprons during calls.

_Sources: [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c8 P20](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0020), [v4 c11 P17](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0017), [v4 c37 P30](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0030)_

## Personality

Miss Cornelia possesses a sharp, bitter tongue combined with an exceptionally kind heart. She is candid, opinionated, and outspoken, harboring a deep disdain for men and Methodists. Despite her crusty exterior and sharp humor, she is deeply compassionate, always rushing to help neighbors in trouble or distress. She values true friendship and recognizes kindred spirits quickly.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P37](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0037), [v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040), [v4 c7 P54](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0054), [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c8 P27](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0027), [v4 c8 P59](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0059)_

## History

Miss Cornelia Bryant lives in an emerald house in Four Winds and is well known throughout the community for her sharp wit, staunch Presbyterianism, and tireless helpfulness. When Anne Blythe moves to Four Winds, Miss Cornelia promptly visits her and recognizes her as a kindred spirit belonging to 'the race that knows Joseph.' She acts as a loyal and devoted friend to Leslie Moore, standing by her through years of hardship. When Gilbert Blythe proposes an operation to cure Dick Moore, Miss Cornelia vehemently opposes the idea out of sympathy for Leslie's plight, though she eventually accepts the outcome when the truth about Dick's identity is revealed. Over the years, she frequently visits Anne and Gilbert, engaging in playful, fiery debates with Captain Jim. Eventually, she astounds her friends by announcing her engagement to Marshall Elliott after he cuts his long-standing beard.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P35](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0035), [v4 c6 P37](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0037), [v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040), [v4 c7 P54](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0054), [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c8 P74](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0074), [v4 c11 P29](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0029), [v4 c18 P15](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0015), [v4 c30 P32](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0032), [v4 c30 P48](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0048), [v4 c32 P2](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0002), [v4 c37 P0](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0000), [v4 c37 P9](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0009), [v4 c37 P10](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0010)_

## Background by volume

- She was an only child for eight years before her brother was born  <sub>[v4 c34 P26](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0026)</sub>
- Her only brother died years prior  <sub>[v4 c28 P7](../source/v04-c28.md#nw-v04-c28-p0007)</sub>
- Won first prize for lemon pies at the Charlottetown Exhibition  <sub>[v4 c10 P35](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0035)</sub>
- Has lived as a lifelong Presbyterian in Four Winds  <sub>[v4 c6 P37](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0037), [v4 c28 P7](../source/v04-c28.md#nw-v04-c28-p0007), [v4 c37 P20](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0020)</sub>

## Quotes

> I'm the best sewer in these parts. I ought to be! Lord, I've done more of it than if I'd had a hundred children of my own, believe ME!  <sub>[v4 c8 P27](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0027)</sub>

> Lord, dearie, I don't hate them. They aren't worth it. I just sort of despise them.  <sub>[v4 c8 P59](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0059)</sub>

> Not that I've many—none nearer than second cousins. I'm a kind of lonely soul, Mrs. Blythe.  <sub>[v4 c8 P76](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0076)</sub>

> I'm not hankering after the vote, believe ME. I know what it is to clean up after the men.  <sub>[v4 c15 P37](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0037)</sub>

> When a thing has to be I give in to it. But I like to make mighty sure first that it HAS to be.  <sub>[v4 c30 P48](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0048)</sub>
